## Summary

This document presents the request for the addition of host countries to FP086 (Green Cities Facility) originally approved at the twenty-first meeting of the Board for the consideration of the Board.

### III. Assessment

The request from the accredited entity that will enable it to expand the programme is part of a set of programmes changes to allow EBRD to accelerate the deployment of the programme, while due diligence on other identified projects continues. The Secretariat is supporting the expansion of the programme by facilitating the inclusion of additional countries under the programme such that the programme can achieve its target outcomes and objectives.

The accredited entity, in consultation with the NIBs of the host countries, has sought to include additional countries as part of this process. These are the same countries with which NIBs of all current host countries (see annex II and annex V). The accredited entity has received seven NIBs from the nine existing host countries, and six additional NIBs from the Secretariat recommend that the Board take note of the inclusion and approve the request.

## Engagement with NDAIs

The EBRO has engaged with the NDAs of the Facility’s host countries to inform and consult them on the changes identified. NDAs welcomed and supported the suggested changes.

Following the submission of the restructuring proposal on 18 July 2022, the EBRO proceeded with formal engagement with the NDAIs, which resulted in a number of proposed changes. The EBRO has agreed to issue new no-objection letters based on the understanding that some of the proposed changes would quality as major changes.

Since then, the EBRO has maintained communication with all the NDAs, in writing, as well as direct interactions via phone calls and meetings.

As a result, seven existing Host Countries have shared new no-objection letters. The NDAs of the other existing Host Countries have expressed their intention to share NDAIs and are proceeding with internal approval processes.

281 The Thai Rice Project addresses mitigation and adaptation priorities identified by the government of Thailand in its NDC and the SAP. It targets a key economic sector – rice farming – that is emissions-intensive and especially vulnerable to climate change. The Thai Rice Project builds on a strong baseline of existing policies, programs, and practices for sustainable agriculture and climate-smart rice farming from a diverse set of public and private sector actors in order to address an identified set of barriers. The project will generate significant co-benefits through the mobilization of substantial additional funding from the private sector, involving actors along the entire value chain.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V10.0 | PAGE 48

## Barriers for Service Providers

### Climate-smart rice farming is at its nascent stage in Thailand: aspects of the emission and/or mitigation potential of climate-smart farming have been posted or synthesised, rolled-out by foundation projects, but baseline projects, but they have not been promoted and disseminated at a large scale nor in an integrated manner. The lack of awareness among farmers about the benefits of climate-smart technology and equipment carries substantial risk due to the unclear business case (particularly for smallholder farmers) compared with the well-established and well-understood sugar cane service provider sector. There is also a perception that the climate-smart rice service provision model is not financially viable, compared with the well-established and well-understood sugar cane service provider sector.

## Assessment of the independent Technical Advisory Panel

### 1. Overview

#### 1.1 Overview

This is a five-year project on rice farming in Thailand, targeting 21 provinces in the three most important rice-growing regions of the country: the north, the northeast and the east (see map). The project will be implemented by the Department of Agriculture for rice farming in Thailand. As such, it is a cross-cutting, medium-term project with a dual objective:

(a) To adapt rice farming in Thailand to order to reduce the negative impacts of observed and anticipated climate change conditions; and

(b) To reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from rice farming in order to help mitigate climate change.

## The Thai Rice Project Will

The Thai Rice Project will enable climate-smart rice farmers—increasingly, women farmers—to adapt to a changing climate (Outcome 1) while simultaneously reducing GHG emissions (Outcome 2).

### Project Design and Outcomes

#### Bottom-up Approach
- **Behavioral Changes**: Triggered at the level of the farmer through behavioral changes.
- **Adoption of Climate-smart Practices**: Climate-smart practices (Output 1.1) and climate-smart technologies will be made available by service providers—industrialized, mechanized, and well-equipped service providers supported by a strong institutional framework.

#### Financial Support
- The climate-smart rice that is produced will be verified and sold at higher market prices.
- A financial support mechanism will be established to ensure the sustainability of this sector, designed and implemented to unlock additional revenue flows to support Thailand’s transition towards a low-carbon economy (Outcome 3).
